candidateClaims.statement: A committed payment state change and an event awaiting publication can be recorded in one database transaction, then relayed to the broker.
conditions: The local payment state and outbox entry share a transactional store.
An asynchronous handoff is justified by the payment workflow.
limitations: Duplicate publication or delivery can still occur; consumers need idempotency.
This does not atomically commit a remote settlement or replace reconciliation.

architectureUnit.mechanism: Commit a state change and an outbox record together, then publish committed records with a monitored relay.

effects.rationale: Avoids an untracked gap between committing state and requesting publication, if the transaction and relay behave as assumed.
A relay, backlog, retry, and duplicate policy require ownership and monitoring.

obligations.action: Test failure immediately before and after commit and relay publication
obligations.evidence: Source-row audit, broker publication log, duplicate-processing result, and reconciliation record for the same payment reference

exclusions: No shared local transaction for the state and outbox record

candidateClaims.statement: Kafka can support independent consumers revisiting retained event records using their positions, subject to the configured retention and consumer design.
conditions: Replay is a stated requirement for the payment investigation or reconstruction use case.
The topic retains the required history and an approved consumer can reset or seek safely.
limitations: Retention and partitioning must be configured and evidenced.
Broker semantics do not alone make writes to an external ledger exactly once.

architectureUnit.mechanism: Partitioned retained log with consumer-managed positions.

effects.rationale: Retained records can be revisited when an authorised consumer and an adequate retention window are available.
Partitions, offset handling, storage, backlog and access to replay require operational controls.

obligations.action: Exercise consumer crash and controlled replay without an additional debit
obligations.evidence: Retained offset range, consumer configuration, payment reference, ledger reconciliation and observed test run

exclusions: Required replay history exceeds verified retention
Consumer cannot legally or safely replay a payment effect

candidateClaims.statement: A RabbitMQ quorum queue may carry unprocessed payment work with publisher confirms and manual consumer acknowledgements under an approved multi-node topology.
conditions: The requirement is reliable delivery of unprocessed work rather than reconstruction from retained consumed history.
The quorum topology and producer/consumer acknowledgement policy are configured and exercised.
limitations: A confirmed publication does not prove downstream processing or ledger correctness.
Behaviour for the project's exact RabbitMQ 4.0 version must be verified from version-appropriate originals.

architectureUnit.mechanism: Replicated quorum queue with publisher confirms and manual consumer acknowledgements.

effects.rationale: Publication and processing can be acknowledged at their distinct boundaries when configured as assumed.
Retained replay of consumed history requires a separate design or verified stream option.

obligations.action: Test leader loss, redelivery, dead-letter handling and consumer crash
obligations.evidence: Topology and policy settings, publication confirms, consumer processing records, and reconciliation for one payment reference

exclusions: Historical replay of already consumed work is mandatory and no separate history exists

decisionRubric.authority: Evaluation expectations authored for the pilot, not independent expert judgements or production thresholds.
checks: Unreviewed candidates never become Sol or model authority and carry no selection score.
A choice with unknown product version or topology must surface missing context; a version mismatch must not inherit version-specific guidance.
If replay of consumed payment events becomes mandatory, reopen the RabbitMQ work-queue rationale and compare a retained-log or separate history design.
If the end-to-end duplicate-debit target changes, reopen consumer deduplication, transactional boundary and reconciliation tests regardless of broker choice.
No wording implies that a numeric availability, latency, recovery or duplicate-debit target has been achieved without a current relevant observation.
An independent architect decides whether the reviewed case is supported; whole-project SDD approval remains separate.
